captured.platform: Tilda Zero Block + GSAP ScrollTrigger + Lenis

colors.note: reads as ~#151515 under the grain overlay

taste.name: Size instead of weight
taste.trigger: When one typeface had to carry hero, headings, body and labels
taste.decision: Chose a single weight (400) with an 18x size jump between hero and body over a bold/regular pairing
taste.reason: A wide letterform at 180px already fills the screen; making it bold as well would read as shouting, while thin strokes at that size read as calm

taste.name: The scroll is the showreel
taste.trigger: When the studio had to prove it can do motion before showing a single case
taste.decision: Chose a 9000px pinned scene driven by the visitor's own scroll over a static portfolio grid
taste.reason: Someone shopping for an animated site believes what moves under their own finger more than a list of logos
evidence: block of 9000px page height pinned to one screen
word 'Portfolio' pans -5070px then scales 22.4x until the photo inside the letters becomes the frame
cost: about 9 screens of scrolling before the first case text

taste.name: No box around anything
taste.trigger: When listing advantages, prices and reviews
taste.decision: Chose hairline rows and cards separated by 6px joints over elevated cards with shadows
taste.reason: On a grainy near-black ground a shadow has nothing to fall on; lines keep the eye on the words
evidence: advantage rows on an 87px pitch with 1px rules

taste.name: Three warm inks, one of them a pointing finger
taste.trigger: When colouring a dark page that runs 22 screens
taste.decision: Chose cream text plus orange labels plus a coral reserved for start, end and the one action over white text with several accent hues
taste.reason: Cream on near-black glares less over a long scroll, and a colour that appears rarely is read as 'here'
evidence: #EF5143 on 23: hero headline, the footer word, and the 0-rouble consultation card among four price cards
